name: Dark Bluish Violet
lede: Dark Bluish Violet is a muted, dark modifier on [[violet]], scanned from Ridgway's 1912 plates and filed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955 as a moderate violet.

sections.title: A double modifier on violet
sections.body:
The name stacks two modifiers, *dark bluish* plus [[violet]], onto the flower-derived color word rather than naming a separate hue [1]. Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places a hue this dark at plate X, hue 57, a scan of an aged plate and so only approximate; the ISCC-NBS system filed the same chip in 1955 as a moderate violet [1].

Its nearest named neighbors by color distance are [[dusky-violet]], almost the same at 3.2 units, and [[dark-madder-violet]], a touch duller at 3.7 [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color this close to Dark Bluish Violet is moderately rare in our archive: 75 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, about 0.3 percent, rarer than 56 percent of the named colors [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 3.3 times the expected rate, and most often plays a shadow, 48 percent of the time [3]. The earliest match dates to 1401, by Taddeo di Bartolo, 511 years before the name's own 1912 record [3]. That is centuries before the name's own record, a floor on the hue's age, not a first use of either the name or a pigment.

origin.named_after: a double modifier on violet; the choice of "dark bluish" over another pairing is undocumented
